channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Datafolha: 70% veem relação entre Congresso e Lula mais como confronto do que colaboração
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on May 17, 2026 shows that 70% of Brazilians view the relationship between President Lula and Congress as more confrontational than collaborative, compared to only 20% who see greater cooperation. Conducted May 12–13 with 2,004 respondents, the survey also found that Lula’s government receives its highest approval for combating hunger and poverty (13%), while public security is the most criticized area. The poll is registered with TSE under BR-00290/2026.

item.title: Flávio posta texto do Poder360 sobre Lula e marca jornais
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) shared on X a Poder360 report about a December 2024 meeting between Lula and Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro, calling it a 'bomb' and tagging Globo profiles. The report claims Lula advised Vorcaro not to sell Banco Master to BTG Pactual for R$ 1, with attendees including future Central Bank head Gabriel Galípolo and government ministers.

item.title: Democracia Cristã confirma Joaquim Barbosa como pré-candidato à Presidência
item.description: Former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa has been confirmed as the presidential pre-candidate of the Christian Democracy (DC) party following his affiliation with the party. This replaces the earlier pre-candidacy of Aldo Rebelo, who insists on maintaining his bid until the convention, possibly through legal action. DC national president João Caldas stated Barbosa embodies national unity and responds to the Brazilian society's demand for change.

item.title: ELEIÇÕES 2026: Lula, Bolsonaro e os Novos Nomes na Disputa?
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian elections are expected to feature Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Jair Bolsonaro as the main contenders, with potential new names emerging as alternatives in the presidential race. Although the political landscape remains polarized, there are signs of renewal and the rise of figures outside the traditional axis. Candidate definitions will depend on party alliances, popular approval, and judicial decisions that could still affect the eligibility of certain politicians.

item.title: 52% dos brasileiros são contra reduzir penas de condenados no 8 de janeiro, diz Genial/Quaest
item.description: A Genial/Quaest poll conducted from May 8 to 11 reveals that 52% of Brazilians oppose reducing sentences for those involved in the January 8, 2023, coup attempt, while 39% support it. The survey was carried out after Congress overturned President Lula’s veto on the sentencing guidelines bill, which sought to revise penalties for those convicted in the events.

item.title: Lula, idiotas antissistema, povo contra a democracia e quem quer o quê
item.description: Lula argues that democracy has failed by not meeting people's basic aspirations, allowing 'anti-system idiots' to gain applause worldwide. He references Yascha Mounk's 'The People vs. Democracy' to show how independent institutions and trade treaties constrain popular will in favor of economic and social elites, even in established democracies. While noting the cordiality between himself and Trump as a global exception, he warns of authoritarian tendencies masked as liberalism.

item.title: Ex-secretário de Lula é cotado para disputar vaga na Câmara pelo DF
item.description: Former Lula aide Marivaldo Pereira, who served in the Justice Ministry during previous PT governments, is being considered by the PT as a candidate for one of the Distrito Federal’s eight seats in the Chamber of Deputies in 2026. His profile is seen as institutional, with experience in legislative formulation, congressional relations, and access to justice. Ruth Venceremos, a former Secom advisor in the current Lula government and 2022 federal deputy alternate, is also mentioned as a potential candidate, with a background in social activism, communication, and culture, appealing to progressive sectors and social movements.

item.title: “Quem não estiver com Joaquim Barbosa está fora do partido”
item.description: The president of the Christian Democracy party (DC), João Caldas, announced former STF minister Joaquim Barbosa as the party's pre-candidate for president in 2026, replacing Aldo Rebelo due to Rebelo's poor polling performance. Caldas stated there had been an agreement to evaluate candidacy viability and that anyone not supporting Barbosa would be expelled from the party.

item.title: 'Não é caro para os padrões de Hollywood', diz Eduardo Bolsonaro sobre investimento de Vorcaro em 'Dark Horse'
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro defended that the R$ 134 million investment by Banco Master in the film 'Dark Horse', about his father Jair Bolsonaro, is not expensive by Hollywood standards, despite exceeding the budgets of 15 of the last 20 Oscar winners. He denied having spoken with banker Daniel Vorcaro about the project, although he signed an executive producer contract, which he called 'provisional and old', and said he used $50,000 of his own money to secure director Cyrus Nowrasteh.

item.title: Lula sinaliza a aliados querer insistir em Jorge Messias para o STF
item.description: Lula remains committed to Jorge Messias as his nominee for the Supreme Court, despite the Senate's rejection with only 34 votes in favor, claiming the defeat was orchestrated by Davi Alcolumbre to oppose the government. He believes Messias meets the technical qualifications and that the Senate overstepped by rejecting the nomination, though he acknowledges there is currently no political viability to push the appointment. Lula is expected to wait until October 2026 to decide on the vacancy left by Roberto Barroso, and if re-elected, intends to renominate Messias.

item.title: A nova pesquisa presidencial do Datafolha, a primeira após a revelação da relação Flávio/Vorcaro
item.description: Datafolha is conducting a presidential poll from Wednesday to Friday to measure voting intentions following the revelation of the relationship between Flávio Bolsonaro and businessman Vorcaro. Results will be released on Friday, the 22nd, and the article is exclusive to subscribers, requiring registration for full access.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro sobre Vorcaro: ‘Só oferecemos a exposição do filme para ele ser perseguido’
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro denied any quid pro quo in the donation from banker Daniel Vorcaro to the film Dark Horse, stating the offer was only for exposure, which would lead to persecution. He denied direct ties to Vorcaro and said he invested only $50,000 in the film’s early stage, while his brother Flávio Bolsonaro negotiated R$134 million with Vorcaro to finance the production. Federal Police are investigating whether funds were diverted to a U.S.-linked fund tied to Eduardo, used to support his stay in the U.S. after STF blocked his accounts.

item.title: Quaest: 52% dos brasileiros rejeitam redução das penas dos envolvidos no 8 de janeiro
item.description: The Quaest poll shows that 52% of Brazilians oppose reducing the sentences of those involved in the January 8 attacks, while 39% support it and 9% are undecided. Opposition is strongest among non-Lula leftists (72%) and independents (56%), and weakest among Bolsonaro supporters (31%). A majority (54%) believe the Dosimetry Law aims to reduce the sentence of former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Lula usa o Washington Post para seduzir voto moderado no Brasil
item.description: President Lula gave an interview to the Washington Post targeting moderate and independent voters in Brazil, aligning it with his international diplomatic strategy. He aimed to rekindle the democratic appeal that secured his narrow victory over Bolsonaro in 2022, directing the message toward undecided domestic voters.

item.title: Ministro Mauro Vieira vai ao Japão nesta 2ª feira
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira will travel to Japan on May 18, 2026, to attend the first Strategic Dialogue of Chancellors, a mechanism established during President Lula’s visit to Japan in March 2025. He will meet with Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi, sign two treaties on consular assistance and health services for persons with disabilities, and commemorate the 130th anniversary of the Treaty of Friendship, Commerce and Navigation. Bilateral trade reached US$11.6 billion in 2025, a 5% increase from the previous year.

item.title: Crusoé: A alternativa Barbosa e a falência da política brasileira
item.description: The nomination of former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa as a presidential alternative for 2026 is interpreted as a symptom of the Brazilian political system's bankruptcy, reflecting a lack of new and credible leadership. His potential candidacy, already considered in 2018, signals desperation with current political options.

item.title: O limite eleitoral das emendas orçamentárias
item.description: The debate surrounding the 2026 general elections has focused primarily on the presidential race, with little attention given to proportional elections, which are decisive for the balance of power in the next government. Flávio Bolsonaro’s candidacy is under scrutiny due to his involvement with Daniel Vorcaro and the Banco Master case, potentially affecting his electoral viability. The renewal of the Chamber of Deputies is highlighted as a key factor in shaping post-election power dynamics.

item.title: Oposição explora desgaste de Lula em segurança, e governo exalta combate a crimes do 'andar de cima'
item.description: The opposition plans to exploit President Lula's lowest-rated area in public security, according to a Datafolha poll, to attack him in the 2026 campaign. The government, in turn, intends to highlight its actions against organized crime, especially the 'upper echelon,' and the legal frameworks sent to Congress.

item.title: Quaest: 52% dos brasileiros rejeitam redução de pena a golpistas do 8 de janeiro
item.description: 52% of Brazilians oppose reducing penalties for those convicted in the January 8 riots, according to a Quaest poll. Among independent voters, opposition rises to 54%, while 39% support leniency. Bolsonaro supporters mostly favor the measure, whereas non-Lulist left-wing voters reject it more strongly.

item.title: Lula vai indicar Messias… de novo
item.description: President Lula told allies he will insist on renominating Attorney General Jorge Messias to the Supreme Federal Court (STF), despite prior rejection. According to Crusoé, Lula is seeking support amid signs of weakening influence from Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) within the Judiciary. The move reflects the government’s strategy to strengthen its influence over the Court.

item.title: Crises em série com Master interrompem maré positiva de Flávio e testam campanha bolsonarista
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) pre-campaign suffered a setback after three cases linked him to Banco Master, interrupting his positive momentum and forcing him into a defensive stance. This crisis unfolds amid a political reaction from President Lula (PT), who is seeking to regain ground as the Bolsonarist candidate faces mounting challenges.

item.title: “Agora eu sou O cara do imobiliário do Texas”, diz Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro denies any financial or patrimonial link between the Mercury Legacy Trust, his lawyer Paulo Calixto, and the purchase of a Texas home for $753,500, accusing critics of attempting to damage his brother Flávio Bolsonaro's reputation. He claims there is no evidence of wrongdoing and that the allegations are a political 'trap'. The Federal Police are investigating whether part of the R$61 million paid by Daniel Vorcaro to the Havengate Development Fund was used to buy Eduardo's property and support his activities against the STF in the U.S.

item.title: Governo de Minas paga parcela de R$ 104 milhões do Propag à União
item.description: The Minas Gerais government paid the fifth installment of the Propag program, amounting to R$ 103.89 million, on May 15, 2026, bringing total payments under the program to R$ 512.2 million since joining in December 2025. The agreement restructured the state's debt with the Union, setting financial charges at IPCA plus 0% real interest, over a 360-month term, with commitments to contribute 1% of the debt balance annually to the FEF and make equivalent strategic investments. Since January 2019, Minas Gerais has paid R$ 13.42 billion to the Union for state debts, including R$ 6 billion under the Fiscal Recovery Regime (2024-2025).

item.title: Entenda a troca da PF no inquérito do INSS
item.description: The Federal Police changed the coordination of the INSS discount fraud investigation (Operation Sem Desconto) involving Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha). The shift occurred during the plea bargain of Mauricio Camisotti, who offered to return R$ 400 million to public coffers. While the PF calls it administrative, the move sparked criticism in Congress and the STF over lack of prior notice and potential interference in the probe.

item.title: 6x1 entra na reta final na Câmara; Lula anuncia R$ 37 bi da Petrobras
item.description: Deputy Leo Prates is set to present the final report on Wednesday for the PEC proposing a reduction in the workweek from 6x1, following weeks of pressure from unions, businesses, and social media mobilization. President Lula announced a R$ 37 billion investment from Petrobras, tied to the economic development and energy agenda. The debate in the Chamber is entering its final stretch, with direct implications for workers and corporate competitiveness.

item.title: O que disseram Flávio, Eduardo e Mário Frias sobre financiamento de Vorcaro para o filme de Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio, Eduardo Bolsonaro, and Mário Frias have given contradictory statements regarding the financing of the film 'Dark Horse' by banker Daniel Vorcaro, who is imprisoned over alleged billion-dollar fraud schemes. Flávio initially denied any contact with Vorcaro, later admitted lying and cited a confidentiality clause; Eduardo first said he only introduced a lawyer, then acknowledged signing a contract as executive producer; Mário Frias denied Vorcaro's funds were involved, then claimed the legal relationship was with a firm linked to him. At least R$ 61 million of the pledged R$ 134 million has been paid.

item.title: 52% dos brasileiros são contra reduzir penas dos envolvidos no 8 de janeiro, aponta Genial/Quaest
item.description: A Genial/Quaest poll reveals 52% of Brazilians oppose reducing sentences for those involved in the January 8 attacks, while 39% support it. Congress overturned President Lula’s veto on the 'Dosimetria Bill,' which could allow Jair Bolsonaro to progress to semi-open regime in two or three years, despite Lula’s claim that the bill undermines constitutional principles and judicial autonomy.

item.title: Lula se prepara para reenviar indicação de Messias antes das eleições, mas ministro adota cautela
item.description: President Lula intends to resend Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF before the October elections, despite its prior rejection in the Senate and the need to reconcile with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. Messias, currently AGU minister, would only accept a new nomination with strong assurance of approval, having been viewed as a victim of political maneuvering. An alternative appointment to the Ministry of Justice exists but is considered secondary.

item.title: Uma família do barulho
item.description: The post describes a fictional plot in which the Bolsonaro brothers produce a Hollywood film glorifying their father, Jair Bolsonaro, who is imprisoned for attempting a coup, starring an actor who played Jesus Christ, only to be swindled by a corrupt banker. It claims this storyline is less problematic than the real-life actions of Flávio and Eduardo Bolsonaro.

item.title: A nova dor de cabeça que Lula encomendou em Minas Gerais
item.description: Minas Gerais PT leaders warn that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva may need to recalibrate his electoral strategy in the state, as the expectation of running Rodrigo Pacheco as a candidate has not materialized. Tensions between the local PT and the federal government require Lula to make a special effort to realign the party and define a new state-level ticket leader. This situation adds an extra challenge to the 2026 presidential campaign.

item.title: Quaest: 52% são contra redução de penas a envolvidos no 8 de Janeiro
item.description: A Quaest poll shows 52% of Brazilians oppose reducing sentences for those involved in the January 8 attacks, while 39% support it and 9% are undecided. Most respondents believe the Dosimetria Law was approved primarily to benefit former President Jair Bolsonaro (54%), not all convicts (34%). The law, which overrode Lula’s veto, reduces penalties for crowd-related crimes if the defendant did not finance or lead the acts.

item.title: Governo vai pior em segurança e melhor em combate à fome, diz Datafolha
item.description: The Lula government is rated worst in public security (16%), health (15%), and economy (13%), while seen as best in combating hunger and misery (13%), unemployment (10%), and education (10%). For the next president, health is the top priority (34%), followed by education (15%), public security (12%), and economy (11%).

item.title: PT e líderes do governo Lula unificam discursos para atacar bolsonarismo
item.description: The PT and Lula’s government leaders intensified attacks on PL’s pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, leveraging his alleged connection to Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, as a political weapon. The strategy includes spreading content on social media, coining the term 'Bolsomaster' to link the Bolsonaro family to the financial scandal, and calling for investigations and preventive detention. Despite lacking concrete evidence, the PT aims to damage Flávio Bolsonaro’s image, who is technically tied with Lula in polling.

item.title: Centrais sindicais fazem Dia Nacional de Lutas pelo fim da 6x1 na véspera de votação na Câmara
item.description: Brazilian trade unions are calling for a National Day of Struggle this Sunday (24) in all state capitals to demand the end of the 6x1 work schedule. The mobilization takes place on the eve of the vote on the proposal in the Chamber of Deputees, highlighting the growing debate over working hours in the context of the 2026 elections. The movement aims to unite workers and popular sectors in defense of reducing the weekly workload.

item.title: Governo Lula vai mal nas áreas que são prioridade para a população, mostra Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha survey shows that the areas where President Lula's government received the worst evaluations — public security (16%), health (15%), and economy (13%) — are exactly the same areas the public considers top priorities for the next government. Health leads priorities at 34%, followed by education (15%), public security (12%), and economy (11%). Conversely, the government was best rated for combating hunger and misery (13%), unemployment and education (10% each).

item.title: Joaquim Barbosa é anunciado como pré-candidato à Presidência pelo Democracia Cristã; Aldo Rebelo sai
item.description: Former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa has been announced as the pre-candidate for President of Brazil by the Christian Democracy party for the 2026 elections, marking his official entry into the race. Simultaneously, Aldo Rebelo was removed from the pre-candidacy, signaling a strategic shift within the party. This development unfolds amid a polarized political landscape and an ongoing search for alternatives beyond the two dominant political blocs.

item.title: Lula deve reenviar nome de Jorge Messias ao STF após derrota no Senado, dizem aliados
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva intends to resend Jorge Messias’ nomination to the Supreme Federal Court to the Senate, despite its prior rejection. Allies say Lula views the episode as an institutional affront by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, not a personal defeat for Messias. The move reflects a strategy of political confrontation with Congress, avoiding the appearance of retreat and upholding the presidential prerogative to appoint STF justices.

item.title: Lula aconselhou Vorcaro a não vender Master ao BTG
item.description: President Lula advised Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, to reject a symbolic offer to sell the bank to BTG Pactual for R$ 1 during a meeting at the Palácio do Planalto on December 4, 2024. Lula urged Vorcaro to keep the bank independent, criticizing Roberto Campos Neto and André Esteves, and emphasizing the goal of reducing banking concentration in Brazil. The decision was reinforced by the presence of Gabriel Galípolo, the new central bank president, and supported by a rise in meetings between Master and the BC under his leadership.

item.title: CPI do Banco Master seguirá ordem regimental, afirma Hugo Motta
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta stated that the request for a Parliamentary Inquiry Committee (CPI) to investigate Banco Master will be analyzed according to the Chamber's internal rules, without specifying what that entails. Currently, seven CPI requests related to the bank are pending in Congress, including one in the Chamber, and two new requests were filed following a report alleging that Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro financed Flávio Bolsonaro’s film about Jair Bolsonaro, with at least $10.6 million paid between February and May 2025.

item.title: O livro que quer trazer segurança digital para o centro do debate
item.description: The book 'Humanity and Digital Power,' launched by Eduardo Felipe Matias, analyzes the political, social, and legal effects of technological transformation. It emerges amid growing digital governance efforts in Brazil and abroad, including new ECA Digital rules, AI regulations in elections, and global measures against deepfakes and online risks to minors.

item.title: Avaliação do governo Lula é pior em áreas prioritárias para eleitor, como segurança, diz Datafolha
item.description: The Datafolha poll shows that President Lula's government receives its worst evaluations in the areas voters consider most important: public security (16%), health (15%), economy (13%), and fight against corruption (13%). These same areas were cited as top priorities for the next president, with health leading at 34%, followed by education (15%), public security (12%), and economy (11%). Among Lula voters, 18% point to security as the main problem, while among Flávio Bolsonaro supporters, fighting corruption is the top criticism at 17%.

item.title: Lula diz ter pedido a Trump fim das sanções a Cuba
item.description: Lula said he personally asked Donald Trump to end U.S. economic sanctions on Cuba, stating the island 'needs a chance'. The request was made during an interview with The Washington Post, published this Sunday, the 17th. He argued that U.S. openness could benefit the Cuban people.

item.title: Lula ofereceu ajuda a Trump para negociar com Irã e pediu fim do bloqueio a Cuba
item.description: Lula offered to help Trump mediate a deal with Iran, sharing a copy of the 2010 Tehran Agreement, which proposed the peaceful use of enriched uranium. He also urged Trump to lift the U.S. commercial embargo on Cuba, saying the country deserves a chance, and received Trump’s assurance that there would be no invasion of the island.

item.title: Lula tem pior avaliação em segurança, saúde e corrupção, diz Datafolha
item.description: The Datafolha poll from May 2026 shows President Lula’s government receiving its worst ratings in public security (16%), health (15%), economy and corruption fight (13%), according to Brazilian voters. Conversely, the government is viewed most favorably in combating hunger and misery (13%), unemployment (10%), and education (10%). The survey interviewed 2,004 people aged 16+ between May 12–13, 2026, with a 2-point margin of error.

item.title: Segurança é área com pior avaliação no governo Lula, aponta Datafolha
item.description: According to Datafolha, public security is the area with the worst evaluation of Lula's government, cited by 16% of respondents as having unsatisfactory performance. Health and economy follow, with 15% and 13% negative evaluations, respectively. Negative perception is concentrated in areas considered priorities by the electorate.

item.title: Datafolha: governo Lula vai pior em segurança e melhor no combate à fome, dizem eleitores
item.description: According to a Datafolha survey released on May 16, voters rate Lula's government best in combating hunger and misery (13%), followed by unemployment and education (10% each). Public security is the worst-rated area (16%), followed by health (15%), economy and corruption fight (13% each). Health is cited as the top priority for the next president.

item.title: Lula diz ter pedido a Trump derrubada de sanções econômicas a Cuba
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said he asked Donald Trump to lift U.S. economic sanctions on Cuba, stating the island 'needs a chance' and that the Cuban government is willing to negotiate. Lula also praised his May 7 meeting with Trump at the White House as positive, emphasizing Brazil’s role as an international mediator and reiterating his opposition to U.S. interventions in Venezuela and Iran, while describing the Palestine conflict as 'genocide'.

item.title: 51% desaprovam o trabalho de Lula e 45%, aprovam, diz Datafolha
item.description: President Lula has 51% disapproval and 45% approval according to a Datafolha poll from May 2026, with 39% rating his government as bad or terrible. Despite initiatives like Desenrola 2.0, the end of the 'blusinhas' tax, and diesel subsidies, negative evaluations persist, suggesting these measures have not yet improved public perception.

item.title: Lula: Trump sabe que "sou melhor do que Bolsonaro"
item.description: Lula stated that Trump already knows he is 'better' than Bolsonaro, emphasizing that he does not need to make any effort for the U.S. president to recognize his superiority. He stressed that political disagreements—such as opposing war with Iran, intervening in Venezuela, and condemning the genocide in Palestine—do not interfere with institutional relations between Brazil and the U.S. Lula also said he believes improved personal rapport with Trump could attract investments and avoid new tariffs on Brazilian goods.

item.title: Datafolha: Segurança e saúde têm pior avaliação no Governo Lula, combate à fome, melhor
item.description: Datafolha survey shows public security (16%) and health (15%) as the worst-rated areas of Lula's third government, while combating hunger and misery (13%) received the best evaluation. The Planalto announced an R$ 11 billion package to fight organized crime, including a proposal to create a Ministry of Public Security if the Security PEC is approved by the Senate. The margin of error is two percentage points.
